content: Furthermore, platforms like TenderBulletins exhibit parallel constraints, as their operational emphasis remains steadfastly on presenting newer developments, such as tenders with grading requirements related to road construction and other infrastructure projects slated for 2026, offering little to no analysis of historical trends [39] . Therefore, synthesizing historical information about engineering tenders and grading requirements from 2020 to 2024 remains highly challenging due to the pervasive lack of retroactive insights across the reviewed platforms [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. In the specific context of structural steel tenders, the procurement landscape as of June 2026 reveals a distinct lack of readily available, up-to-date opportunities tailored precisely to the requirements of this specialized sector [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. A thorough examination of contemporary listings indicates that many advertised tenders either reflect expired opportunities or cover entirely unrelated sectors, such as general construction services or emergency procurement. For instance, while the IDT website featured various advertised tenders, the available information focused predominantly on a panel for general construction services rather than structural steel, rendering the data largely unrelated or outdated due to temporal gaps [36] . Similarly, the Tenders-SA platform, despite describing itself as the most comprehensive tender database in South Africa, provided content that was insufficiently detailed to confirm the presence of active structural steel tenders without requiring direct navigation to their main website for newer postings [37] . EasyTenders, for example, listed a tender closing on June 30, 2026, but the subject matter was centered on aerial firefighting services, making it entirely inapplicable to the structural steel industry [38] . Even platforms more closely aligned with the engineering sector face similar temporal issues; TenderBulletins hosted a dedicated steel structures category, yet detailed a tender that had already closed, failing to outline the precise requirements for structural steel in its available examples [39] . Additionally, GlobalTenders mentioned a steel-related tender for the construction of a perimeter wall in South Africa, but with a deadline of June 25, 2026, the opportunity had already expired at the time of analysis, leaving it inapplicable for stakeholders seeking ongoing or upcoming procurement opportunities [40] .
